Balita

Padala grew 2.7% in September

Overseas Filipinos sent home $3.55 billion in personal remittances in September, up 2.7 percent from $3.46 billion a year earlier and higher than August's $3.37 billion, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) reported. Personal remittances are the broad count: cash through banks, cash through informal channels, and goods sent in kind. Cash remittances, the bank-only count, rose 2.6 percent to $3.2 billion. From January to September, personal remittances reached $29.65 billion, up 2.3 percent. The United States stayed the top source, followed by Singapore and Saudi Arabia. Why it matters: padala equaled 8.4 percent of gross domestic product (the total value of what the economy produces) as of the third quarter, and it keeps household spending going. Economists expect a Christmas lift, but say yearly growth may not speed up because last year's levels were already high. Jonathan Ravelas of Reyes, Tacandong & Co. said the pace will depend on key OFW markets, "particularly the Middle East." The peso has also kept weakening this past month (see the rate box). PhilStar: Remittances rise 2.7% to $3.55 billion

By BSP data, the US accounted for 39.8% of cash remittances, Singapore 7.1% and Saudi Arabia 6.4%, while land-based workers sent 80% and sea-based workers 20%. GMA Money: Cash remittances rose to $3.20B in Sept. 2026 --BSP

Para sa pamilya: Christmas padala season is near: compare your remittance channel's fees now so more of each transfer reaches home.

Balita

Fuel prices drop again today

Pump prices go down again today, Tuesday, November 17, the second straight week of rollbacks (price cuts at the pump). Per the Department of Energy (DOE), gasoline drops P1.50 per liter across all grades, diesel including Diesel Plus drops P3.80, and kerosene drops P5.80. The new prices are expected to hold through Monday, November 23, and the DOE said the cuts must be applied in full. Last week, gasoline fell by P16.80, diesel by P4.10 and kerosene by P3.70. The DOE tied the cuts to the global oil market, which has eased on hopes of talks between the United States and Iran. What is unknown is how long it lasts: an industry source said prices had rebounded recently as attacks on Saudi energy facilities and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz escalated. A weaker peso also makes imported fuel costlier, offsetting some of the relief. The country remains under a state of national energy emergency. PhilStar: Fuel prices to fall again on Nov. 17

GMA carries the DOE's per-liter figures and the industry warning about a possible rebound. GMA Money: Fuel prices to go down anew on November 17

Also reported by Inquirer Business: New round of oil price cuts set this week

Para sa pamilya: From today through Nov. 23, diesel costs P3.80 less per liter, gasoline P1.50 less and kerosene P5.80 less.

Court scraps bond for seafarers

Filipino seafarers who win money in a labor case no longer have to post a bond (a guarantee, usually paid for, that the money will be returned if the ruling is reversed) to collect disputed amounts while an appeal is pending. The Supreme Court struck down that part of the 2024 Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers, saying it unfairly burdened seafarers compared with other workers. Wages, statutory benefits and undisputed amounts were already payable right away. The decision, written by Associate Justice Maria Filomena Singh in the November 11 session and announced November 16, also voided the use of the DMW's AKSYON Fund to pay bond premiums, and struck down the 10% ceiling on lawyers' fees, saying regulating lawyers belongs to the Court. Rules on maritime schools and shipboard training were upheld. The Federation of Free Workers, a petitioner, called it a win: "Tagumpay ito ng mga manggagawa." The coverage does not say how quickly pending cases will apply the ruling. PhilStar: Supreme Court: Seafarers no longer required to post bond for disputed awards

The Court also upheld a ban on charging tuition for shipboard training run by third-party providers. PhilStar: SC: Seafarers' bond for seeking damages unconstitutional

Also reported by Inquirer: SC strikes down unfair provisions in seafarers magna carta

Para sa pamilya: A seafarer with a pending claim no longer pays for a bond to collect disputed awards; the 10% lawyer fee cap is gone, so get fees in writing.

Diskarte

ASEAN pact on fair recruitment

A heads-up, not a to-do: there is nothing to file or claim yet. ASEAN leaders adopted a Philippine-led declaration on fair and ethical recruitment that the DMW says could benefit around 600,000 OFWs in Southeast Asia. It aims to curb excessive recruitment fees, tighten agency licensing and monitoring, open complaint channels and fight cyberscam trafficking. The DMW and the embassy in Yangon are monitoring about 90 to 100 Filipinos allegedly trapped in Myanmar scam compounds. The coverage does not say when member countries will put the rules in place. PhilStar: 600,000 OFWs to benefit from ASEAN migrant worker declaration

Para sa pamilya: If a relative gets a job offer in Southeast Asia, confirm with the DMW that the agency is licensed before paying any fee.
